title: SugarBloom API Surge
text:
SugarBloom API Surge

notes:
Inbound SMB trial. Key points: self-serve signup, one developer ran smoke tests and embeddings, then activity stalled. CTO said 'works for demo but not sure on bills' during 1/12 call. Primary ask was predictable per-session cost and an easy drop-in JS snippet for product recommendations. Risk signals: devs pulled to BrightServe POC that has a 'free tier' experiment; no SSO yet, SOC2/audit logs are requested for later stages. AE Maya reached out 2/18 with re-engagement email; proposing 30-day credit + migration support. Suggested tactics: send tailored cost comparison (per-100k token) + pre-built storefront connector repo, offer 1-hr office hours with Diego. Notes style: terse, follow-up needed. Attachments: pricing deck, quickstart link. Potential close: small monthly committed contract if they get through one holiday spike without cost surprises. 

timeline:
2026-01-05 - inbound signup via docs site, trial key issued automatically
2026-01-07 - initial smoke test: basic chat + embedding call from dev laptop (latency ~120ms)
2026-01-12 - discovery call w/ Maya + Diego; CTO (A. Park) asked about caching and cost controls (Fireflies FF-2026-01-12-4589)
2026-01-20 - follow-up email with sample prompt templates + cost projection sent
2026-02-02 - usage drops to near-zero after first week; devs started testing competitor BrightServe
2026-02-10 - se provided JS snippet for storefront connector; dev reports integration friction
2026-02-18 - trial auto-expiry warning sent; no response from main dev contact

blockers:
stalled after initial API key smoke test
low invocation volume — devs pulled toward competitor POC
unclear pricing fit for bursty store traffic
no easy SDK for their JS storefront connector

next_step:
Re-engagement email + 30d trial credit offer; schedule 20m convo week of 2026-02-24
